scenario: A regional development researcher makes data requests using ambiguous or easily confused geographic terms. They ask for indicators in regions that are commonly conflated, such as South Asia versus Southeast Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa versus all of Africa, Congo without specifying which country, Korea without specifying North or South, and America without clarifying continent versus country. The chatbot must either resolve the ambiguity correctly or ask the user to clarify before fetching data.
expected_outcome: ALL of the following must be achieved before the conversation is complete: (1) The chatbot correctly distinguishes South Asia from Southeast Asia when the user requests South Asian data. (2) The chatbot correctly resolves Sub-Saharan Africa using the SSF region code, excluding North African countries. (3) When the user says "Congo" without qualification, the chatbot either asks which Congo is meant or correctly provides data for the intended country with a note about the ambiguity. (4) When the user says "Korea" or "America," the chatbot disambiguates or asks for clarification. (5) All data responses include claim tags and source citations.

turns.content: Could you please compare these economic indicators for both Congos side-by-side for the years 2021 to 2024?

**Data:** (2021–2024, latest available, annual)

Country codes:  
- Democratic Republic of Congo = **COD**  
- Republic of Congo = **COG**

---

### 1. GDP (current US$)

| Year | D.R. Congo (COD) | Republic of Congo (COG) |
|------|------------------|-------------------------|
| 2024 | <claim id="90de0956" policy="auto">70,962,185,790.71</claim> US$ | <claim id="a5ae2f6d" policy="auto">15,719,986,076.65</claim> US$ |
| 2023 | <claim id="de8b4408" policy="auto">69,843,655,425.29</claim> US$ | <claim id="4350df14" policy="auto">15,321,055,822.52</claim> US$ |
| 2022 | <claim id="6c961153" policy="auto">70,422,346,142.20</claim> US$ | <claim id="bc2761fb" policy="auto">15,817,030,154.69</claim> US$ |
| 2021 | <claim id="972af35d" policy="auto">59,067,289,573.51</claim> US$ | <claim id="819692f4" policy="auto">14,825,690,210.92</claim> US$ |

---

### 2. GDP per capita (current US$)

| Year | D.R. Congo (COD) | Republic of Congo (COG) |
|------|------------------|-------------------------|
| 2024 | <claim id="bb66ffbb" policy="auto">649.38</claim> US$ | <claim id="29293695" policy="auto">2,482.25</claim> US$ |
| 2023 | <claim id="203c05fa" policy="auto">660.21</claim> US$ | <claim id="97c8796c" policy="auto">2,477.98</claim> US$ |
| 2022 | <claim id="5e36694e" policy="auto">687.74</claim> US$ | <claim id="3d642825" policy="auto">2,620.84</claim> US$ |
| 2021 | <claim id="381e2c08" policy="auto">595.74</claim> US$ | <claim id="18c23911" policy="auto">2,516.16</claim> US$ |

---

### 3. Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)

- D.R. Congo (COD): **no WDI observations returned for 2021–2024** under `FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG` in the dataset used here.
- Republic of Congo (COG):

| Year | Inflation (annual %) |
|------|----------------------|
| 2024 | <claim id="c8555a5a" policy="auto">3.09</claim>% |
| 2023 | <claim id="ed4bc7f0" policy="auto">4.30</claim>% |
| 2022 | <claim id="775a0d13" policy="auto">3.04</claim>% |
| 2021 | <claim id="04336779" policy="auto">1.72</claim>% |

---

### 4. Unemployment rate (total, modeled ILO estimate, % of labor force)

| Year | D.R. Congo (COD) | Republic of Congo (COG) |
|------|------------------|-------------------------|
| 2024 | <claim id="2a3c293c" policy="auto">4.56</claim>% | <claim id="3fa7ce03" policy="auto">19.69</claim>% |
| 2023 | <claim id="f45a5e96" policy="auto">4.48</claim>% | <claim id="7ddd039c" policy="auto">19.90</claim>% |
| 2022 | <claim id="5ff66a18" policy="auto">4.52</claim>% | <claim id="57d57a84" policy="auto">20.11</claim>% |
| 2021 | <claim id="7b69877b" policy="auto">5.28</claim>% | <claim id="27ab09cf" policy="auto">21.96</claim>% |

---

### 5. Current account balance (% of GDP)

| Year | D.R. Congo (COD) | Republic of Congo (COG) |
|------|------------------|-------------------------|
| 2024 | <claim id="9124fc81" policy="auto">-3.83</claim>% | — (no data) |
| 2023 | <claim id="d9c79868" policy="auto">-5.56</claim>% | — (no data) |
| 2022 | <claim id="575dc6a9" policy="auto">-4.47</claim>% | — (no data) |
| 2021 | <claim id="1c7860a7" policy="auto">-0.99</claim>% | <claim id="e76ec5ca" policy="auto">11.57</claim>% |

(“—” = not available in this WDI series for that year.)

---

### Analysis (brief comparisons)

- **Size of economy:** D.R. Congo’s GDP is roughly **4–5 times larger** than Republic of Congo’s across 2021–2024.
- **Average income:** Republic of Congo’s GDP per capita (about **US$ 2,500–2,600**) is consistently around **4× higher** than D.R. Congo’s (about **US$ 600–700**).
- **Unemployment:** Modeled unemployment is **low in D.R. Congo (~4–5%)** but **very high in Republic of Congo (~20%)**.
- **External balance:**  
  - D.R. Congo runs **current account deficits** in 2021–2024.  
  - Republic of Congo shows a **large surplus (11.6% of GDP) in 2021**, with no later WDI data in this series.
- **Inflation:** Only Republic of Congo has WDI CPI data here, showing **moderate, single‑digit inflation** (about 2–4%).

---

**Sources:**

- **World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)**  
  - GDP (current US$) — `NY.GDP.MKTP.CD`  
  - GDP per capita (current US$) — `NY.GDP.PCAP.CD`  
  - Inflation, consumer prices (annual %) — `FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG`  
  - Unemployment, total (% of total labor force) (modeled ILO estimate) — `SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS`  
  - Current account balance (% of GDP) — `BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS`  

---

**Suggested follow-ups:**

1. Can you plot these indicators for both countries on charts for 2000–2024 to see long‑term trends?  
2. Can you add population and poverty rates to compare social outcomes between the two countries?  
3. Can you pull inflation for D.R. Congo from IMF data so we can compare inflation across both countries?
